blocks.text: The module documentation describes the run-chain model, recording link, queue behavior, approvals, modes, and folder trust. Imports then connect the controller to device, policy, tool, checkpoint, store, and rendering layers.
blocks.title: Session responsibilities and safety rules

blocks.text: Small dataclasses represent approval, domain, and modal prompts. Session validates mode, builds the project context and trust state, creates the conversation record, and initializes link, runner, queue, and lifecycle state.
blocks.title: Controller state and construction

blocks.anchor: async def start(self, connect_timeout_s: float = 15.0) -> int | None:
blocks.text: start creates callbacks, connects the device, handles revocation and reachability failures, and starts the worker. run wraps UI execution, while close cancels work, closes the runner and proxy, and shuts down the link.
blocks.title: Link startup and shutdown

blocks.text: The UI-facing methods expose prompt state, capture approval/domain/grant keys, submit messages to the queue, handle escape and interrupts, cycle modes, complete file mentions, and interpret slash commands.
blocks.title: Input routing and commands

blocks.text: Trust properties and methods decide whether project settings can be loaded, show the startup question, remember answers, and re-check fingerprints. _read_existing uses the path guard and no-follow file opening for bounded diffs.
blocks.title: Folder trust and safe file reads

blocks.anchor: def _log(self, kind: str, data: dict) -> None:
blocks.text: Results and checkpoints are recorded in the conversation store. Link callbacks log proposed calls, render events, update run state, handle errors, and react to connection loss without allowing callback exceptions to kill the connection.
blocks.title: Logging and device callbacks

blocks.text: Approval memory can answer repeated calls without prompting, while active approval and domain state feed UI decisions. Network prompts are serialized and moved onto the terminal loop; proxy decisions are recorded with bounded metadata.
blocks.title: Approval and network prompts

blocks.text: The worker drains queued text, starts runs as needed, logs user events, sends messages, and marks rejected sends as unsent. Starting rebuilds bounded history into a new server run; cancellation interrupts the runner and waits briefly for terminal confirmation.
blocks.title: Message delivery and run lifecycle

blocks.anchor: def _rewind_steps(self) -> list[tuple[int, str, str, int, list[str]]]:
blocks.text: The controller lists checkpoint steps without file contents, asks for a numbered choice and confirmation, then cancels the run and restores files through the checkpoint subsystem. It reports restored, deleted, unchanged, skipped, and failed items.
blocks.title: Checkpoint rewind

blocks.text: _grant serializes requests for additional credits, displays the result, ends a run that disappeared, and refreshes status.
blocks.title: Budget grant request

gotchas: A paused or interrupted run is ended before the next message starts a new run from rebuilt history.
Project settings are loaded only after a stable trust fingerprint check before and after reading them.
The local log records event metadata and content needed for history, but callback failures are reduced to type-only diagnostics.

purpose: Session is the client-side controller behind the terminal chat and deliberately contains no terminal rendering implementation. It connects asynchronous server events and user input to the local store, policy, tool, trust, checkpoint, and network-prompt components.
summary: Coordinates the terminal chat UI, device link, tool runner, trust prompts, runs, approvals, and rewinds.
